clue.text: Rubber sheet?

parts.note: crepe is a crinkled rubber used for shoe soles, and the same crinkled texture names a sheet of decorative craft paper

explanation.surface: A waterproof mattress cover, of the kind made of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rubber bedsheet; the question mark points to a sheet of paper with the crinkled finish shared by crepe rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: Crinkled tissue used for decorations has the same puckered texture as the crepe rubber of shoe soles.

clue.text: Check out cross breed of cattle

indicators.note: the word for check is spread out so that it sits outside the cross

parts.note: to check is to deter or hold back
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and look at a cross-bred cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' reads as one phrase meaning examine, but 'out' tells you DETER goes round X.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is a small hardy cattle breed originating in Ireland.

clue.text: On track?

parts.note: read 'on' as switched on, electrified, and the track as a railway

explanation.surface: A question asking whether things are going to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On track' usually means progressing well; here 'on' means carrying current, as the electrified third rail of a railway does.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrified conductor rail carries current alongside the running rails of a railway line.

clue.text: Females coming into a fortune? What nonsense

indicators.note: the females enter the middle of the word for a fortune

parts.note: a pile is a large amount of money
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A scornful retort to the idea of women inheriting a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming into a fortune' reads as inheriting money, but it is the container signal: the females go inside the word for a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish, the same as saying 'What nonsense!'

clue.text: Academic review one's written about German composer

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, an academic

indicators.note: the review and the one are written around the German

parts.note: to scan is to look over or review
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A scholar's critique of a German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German composer' looks like one phrase, but 'German' gives G, placed inside SCANI; Pietro Mascagni was in fact Italian, composer of Cavalleria Rusticana.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Mascagni was an Italian opera writer, best known for Cavalleria Rusticana.

clue.text: Slovenian lake shown in British Library edition

parts.note: BL is the standard abbreviation for the British Library

explanation.surface: A Slovenian lake featured in a British Library publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Bled is an Alpine lake in north-west Slovenia with a church on its island.

clue.text: Instruct fellow to go off for cheese

indicators.note: the fellow is told to leave, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to brief someone is to instruct them

explanation.surface: Telling a man to fetch some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' hints at cheese going bad; it tells you to remove F from BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Paradoxically I call Roy in for training

indicators.note: the words are put through training, drilled into a new formation

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone oddly summons Roy in for a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For training' signals an anagram of I CALL ROY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening in a way contrary to what was expected.

clue.text: Bird's unusual cry he reacts to

indicators.note: the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird's strange call that a man responds to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' signals an anagram of CRY HE REACTS TO; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black-and-white wading bird of the shore with a long orange bill.

clue.text: Fail to notice as much, being pure

parts.note: to spot something is to notice it
together with 'as much', failing to notice as much means noticing less

explanation.surface: Overlooking things in order to stay unsullied.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split as an instruction: 'spot less' means notice less, that is fail to notice as much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no stain or blemish is clean and pure.

clue.text: Flyer's taken in by brave front

indicators.note: the flyer is held inside the word for brave

parts.note: to face danger is to brave it
a flyer is a leaflet advertisement, an ad; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A pilot fooled by a courageous show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot, but it is a printed leaflet, an AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, and by extension an outward show.

clue.text: Militaristic state to scrap volunteer force

parts.note: to spar is to scrap or fight
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army

explanation.surface: A warlike nation deciding to abolish its reserve army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as abolish; it means fight, SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was famed for its harsh military discipline.

clue.text: Seeing foreign monarch going inside causes stir

indicators.note: the monarch is placed inside the scrambled letters
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A visiting foreign king makes waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' scrambles the first word, giving ENGISE, and 'going inside' slots the queen's cipher in after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone is to rouse them into activity, to put vigour into them.

clue.text: Apply touch of grease to rickety stern, then reinforce

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and unsound, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a touch is a small amount, here just the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to lubricate a shaky boat's stern before shoring it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch of grease' gives G, which joins STERN THEN, and 'rickety' scrambles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to make it stronger and more robust.

clue.text: Public transport?

parts.note: read 'public' as the populace, folk in general, and 'transport' as a vehicle that conveys them

explanation.surface: A question about buses and trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'public' means people and the phrase names a large family car.
explanation.definitionFit: A large car seating seven or so, used for carrying many folk at once, is a vehicle that transports the public.

clue.text: Singles on tax officer for tete-a tete

parts.note: a single is a one; plural singles gives two of them
TO stands for tax officer
a single is a one; plural singles gives two of them

explanation.surface: Unattached people meeting a taxman for a private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singles' gives two ones, either side of the tax officer; 'on' is a link, with the pieces stacked in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people is a meeting face to face, just the pair of them.

clue.text: Edge along the way

parts.note: a margin running beside a highway, the strip at the side of a street

explanation.surface: Moving forward gradually on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge along' suggests creeping forward; read 'edge' as a noun and 'way' as a street.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge or margin beside a highway is the strip at its side.

clue.text: Key in design detail to produce object

indicators.note: the key is placed inside the design-and-detail pair

parts.note: design is a form of art
a fact is a detail or particular
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Typing in the specifics of a design to create something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key in' suggests typing; 'key' is a musical note, and 'in' slots it between the two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made object, especially one of historical interest, is an artefact.

clue.text: Knowing when to express disapproval over European

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over the European

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to tut is to make a clicking sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Being shrewd about when to criticise a European.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, sharp-witted and perceptive.

clue.text: Top rate sure to increase

parts.note: A is a top grade or rating, as in A1
if you are bound to do something, you are sure to

explanation.surface: The highest tax band is certain to go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top rate' suggests tax; it is the top grade, A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be plentiful, to multiply in great numbers.

clue.text: Give out number when turning up punctually

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: Distributing a figure when one arrives promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reads as arriving; it reverses EMIT and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at the scheduled hour means arriving promptly.

clue.text: Bill's given price to go up to

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
a price is a cost

explanation.surface: A man named Bill told a price to raise it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go up to' reads as raising a price; it means approach someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly.

clue.text: Keen to appear aloof

definitions.meaning: a keen wind is a biting, chilly one

explanation.surface: Eager to look standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen wind is biting and chilly, and an unfriendly, distant person is described the same way.

clue.text: Show indecision when one's in hospital property

indicators.note: the one is placed inside the hospital-and-property pair

parts.note: an estate is a piece of property
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Dithering when one is on hospital grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into ESTATE after the S, with H in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause or waver before acting is to display uncertainty.

clue.text: Under it all, terribly spiteful

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Underneath everything, someone is really mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' reads as an intensifier; it scrambles UNDER IT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-tempered and malicious, with an unkind disposition.

clue.text: Deal with it in the same ethical manner

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Tackle the matter with equally principled behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'saME ETHical'.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a problem is to face and handle it.
